summary: Expert agents decode Mulham Trading "Best 1-Min Scalping Strategy" + design an HONESTLY-validated M1 scalp archetype for FRIDAY (OOS + real spread, no hindsight)

spec.risk_exits:
SL/TP/TRAILING — structure-anchored, spread-netted, reusing dynamic_stop.py verbatim:

STOP: SL is the swept-wick extreme ± buffer (returned by the entry fn as sl_px). For the live order, widen it with the genome floor via the EXISTING `dstop.dynamic_sl_distance(high,low,close,direction,entry,base_atr_mult=stop_atr,atr=a)` — which already does structure(swing)+momentum, floor=genome base, cap 2.5x. Floor grid `stop_atr ∈ {1.4,1.8,2.2}` (report 4; live evolver already converged to 1.8). NEVER tighter than 1.4xATR on M1 — a tighter stop is pure noise+spread death.

SPREAD-NET (the make-or-break, non-negotiable): effective_risk = SL_dist + spread; effective_reward = TP_dist − spread; the backtest charges this automatically — `cost_R = spread_arr[i]/atr` is ALREADY subtracted per trade in genome_factory._bt_fast (line 86/100) and market_gate.backtest (line 136). For M1 honesty I ADD a slippage+commission pad: change cost to `(spread_arr[i] + 2*slip_pts*point)/(stop*atr) + commission_R`. Do NOT weaken this — it is what kills the strategy honestly.

TP / R:R: TP = R_MULT × net-risk, capped at the next opposing session extreme (the "next liquidity pool" — TP=box's opposite edge / prior opposite-session level). R_MULT grid `{2.0,2.5,3.0}`, start 2.0. HARD RULE: reject any (symbol,session) cell whose net R after spread < 1.6 — a 52% trigger only survives on RR, never on hit-rate. This directly answers the live evolver's failure: its target_atr maxes at 2.0 vs stop 1.8 ≈ 1.1 raw R, which is BELOW the spread cost — that is why all 44 trades net -29.66R. The fix hypothesis = R≥2.0 NET, not raw.

TRAILING: do NOT trail until +1.0R net (premature trailing on M1 = stopped by spread wobble). After +1.0R use `dstop.dynamic_manage(high,low,close,learned_be,learned_trail)` → momentum-scaled BE(0.20→0.45 ATR) + trail(1.0→1.8 ATR), ratchet-only. Scale out 50% at +1.0R, move SL to BE+spread, runner trails.

TIME-STOP: max_hold grid {90,150,240,360}s, start 150 (live evolver runs 90 and bleeds; M1 sweeps resolve 1-3 min). Rule: if not ≥+0.5R by max_hold → close; never time-stop a trade already ≥+0.5R.

SESSION FILTER (the ONLY OOS-proven edge in the repo — memory: −$18 all-hours → +$904 PF 3.36 excluding 22:00-08:00 UTC): TRADE only NY_OVERLAP(13-17 UTC) + LONDON(8-13); DEMOTE NY_LATE (conf+0.05, R≥2.5); HARD-BLOCK ASIAN + TRANSITION as a non-negotiable veto (NOT a tunable). Wiring is free: `multi_trader._genomes()` already SKIPS a symbol whose stable has no specialist for the current session — so emit specialists ONLY for the allowed sessions and the router enforces discipline automatically. Gold = NY-only per memory.

NEWS/SPREAD VETO: honor news_blocked_symbols.json (already read by _agent_inputs); add spread-spike proxy — skip if current spread > 2× trailing-20-bar median OR > SPREAD_MAX[sym]. RAILS kept: −15% daily kill (coordinator shared floor), hard SL on EVERY order (never the no-stop pattern that caused the −$2156 stacker blowup).
spec.oos_gate:
THE GATE IT MUST PASS BEFORE LIVE (reuse the existing engine, raise the M1 bars):

METHOD (already built, do not reinvent): no-lookahead walk-forward, decision at bar i uses close[:i+1], outcome on i+1.. only, OOS = last 55%, 4 folds, REAL per-bar spread from each bar's MT5 'spread' field (genome_factory._real_spread_price, never zero). Plug the archetype in by threading an `arch` param through `_vote_series`/`_bt_fast` (factory) and `backtest`/`_vote` (gate): when arch=="mulham_sweep", per-bar signal = mulham_sweep_m1() instead of the 21-indicator _vote.

TWO SMALL CODE EDITS (the only real changes):
  1. genome_factory.py:27 → TFS=["M1","M5","M15","H1"] (or a separate M1-only run so it doesn't slow the 3h grid).
  2. market_gate.py:176 tfmap → add "M1": mt5.TIMEFRAME_M1.
Plus: pull DEEP history (BAR_WINDOWS=[50000] like the session-specialist path) so each of the 4 folds gets ≥25 M1 trades.

PASS BAR (ALL must hold, POST-COST — stricter than the default gate for an M1 claim):
  • trades ≥ 100  (raise MIN_TRADES 30→100 for M1; M1 has the bars, and statistical weight demands it)
  • profit_factor ≥ 1.2  AND  net_R > 0  (after real spread + slippage pad + commission)
  • folds_pos ≥ 3 of 4  (anti data-mining, already enforced)
  • net R-per-trade ≥ 1.6 after cost  (the report-4 hard floor)
  • Deflated Sharpe > 0.5: feed per-trade returns (factory already stores returns[-300:]) to quant_gates.deflated_sharpe_ratio(returns, n_trials) where n_trials = total grid combos tried (stop×tgt×gate×bars×confirm×session — large, so DSR sets a high bar precisely to kill grid-search luck). write_best() already calls PSR/DSR; just pass n_trials honestly.
  • ADVERSARIAL: must survive adversarial_backtest spread_2x transform (the spread-widen transform is THE killer — gold overlay went PF1.32→0.50 at 3x). If it dies at 2x spread it is not deployable.
  • REPORT median_cost_R explicitly — expect ~0.4-0.6 on XAU M1; that single number is the verdict.

A PASS only makes it ELIGIBLE. Then forward-prove: route through paper_prover.py (forward, no order_send, no auto-promote) + scalp_proof (≥50 real demo trades, PF≥1.2, net>0) → PROVEN (needs explicit user approval). Same promotion path the session specialists already use — no new governance.
spec.integration:

(A) GENOME ARCHETYPE = "MULHAM_SWEEP" (the learnable, OOS-gated path): add an `archetype` field to the genome config schema (default "consolidated_vote"; new "mulham_sweep"). multi_trader._genomes() reads via .get() with defaults so OLD genomes keep working — no schema break. Build it through the EXISTING build_session_specialists() (it already reuses _bt_fast and writes data/genomes/<SYM>/<SESSION>.json + stable.json), so you get per-session sweep genomes for free, and the session router (multi_trader.py:72-77) routes/benches them automatically. Extend the GA grid with archetype params: sweep_session, sweep_confirm ∈ {body_close, ifvg, wick_reject}, sweep_confirm_bars ∈ {1..5}, sweep_sl_buffer_atr, R_MULT — let GA pick per symbol×session.

(B) LIVE ENTRY-MODE in multi_trader.cycle() (mirror the existing dive/wick-rev/gap blocks): when the routed genome's archetype=="mulham_sweep", call the detector on M1 fast rates; if it fires, set reason="mulham-sweep", conf=WICK_REV_CONF(0.70), and EITHER fire market on the reclaim OR arm a retest pending at the box edge via the existing _place_pending() (model the rectangle as the PendingPlan with gap_lo/gap_hi = box bounds — fvg_pending.PendingPlan already has exactly these fields). Register "mulham_sweep" in the _mode_weights() live-P&L map so a losing sweep mode gets benched on real money like dive/wick/gap.

SEEDING: register MULHAM_SWEEP ONLY for GOLD + NY_OVERLAP first (then LONDON), magic = a dedicated new id (e.g. 99794, distinct from the 99791 scalper). It competes in the twin-gene tournament against the incumbent WICK_REV_CONF genome; if it doesn't beat it on post-spread expectancy, it stays benched. DRY_RUN/min-lot/PAPER until it clears the full gate. The reflection-engine scalp tunables (scalp_min_confidence etc.) tune it live ONLY after it passes.
spec.verdict:
BRUTALLY HONEST: I'd bet AGAINST a real edge on M1, and the strongest evidence is FRIDAY's own data, not the video. The live scalp_evolver_state.json I just read shows 44 trades, net_total −29.66R, and EVERY single knob value across all 7 knobs carries a NEGATIVE EWMA (best −0.68). That is a measured, after-cost verdict that the current M1 scalp has NO edge — it is a net loser. The convergent priors all point the same way: memory records SMC CISD/CHoCH ~50% = hindsight, IFVG ~52% on trial; Mulham's M1 trigger IS the IFVG/CISD body-close, so its honest no-lookahead hit-rate is ~52% — a coin flip that can only survive on RR.

THE SPREAD MATH IS THE KILLER: on XAU M1, ATR(14) is ~$0.30-0.80; a 1.8xATR stop ≈ 55-145 points; realistic XAUUSDm demo spread is ~15-35 pts (50-200+ on news). cost_R = spread/(stop×ATR) ≈ 0.4-0.6R EVERY trade. A true 52%/1:1 strategy (raw expectancy ~+0.06R) becomes ~−0.4R after cost — spread is 5-7x the raw edge. That single arithmetic is why the evolver bleeds, and it is structural, not a tuning miss.

WHAT IS REAL: NOT the rectangle entry. The ONE genuinely OOS-validated edge in this whole repo is BEHAVIORAL — session discipline: the user's real manual record flips −$18 → +$904 (PF 3.36) purely by excluding 22:00-08:00 UTC. So the deployable value of "applying Mulham" is the session-gated, structure-stopped, R≥2.0-net DISCIPLINE wrapper, with the sweep entry on probation underneath it.

PREDICTION (and the deliverable): run it through the gauntlet on M1 explicitly and expect "direction ~52% OOS, median_cost_R ~0.4-0.6, net_R<0, DSR<0.5 → REJECTED by market_gate." That documented rejection line in market_gate.json is exactly what an honest shop wants on its books. The ONLY plausible survivor is the SAME setup on M5/M15 during NY/London on gold or a trend-clean index (US30) — where the ATR/spread ratio is sane — but that is then a SLOWER strategy, no longer a "1-minute" one. RECOMMENDATION: build the archetype as specified (cost is ~3 small edits since every primitive already exists), gate it on M1, let the spread kill it on the record, and ship ONLY whatever (if anything) survives on M5/M15 NY-gold/indices. NEVER relax the M1 cost model to force a pass. Burden of proof is on the strategy; the prior is that it fails.
